steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Eastern Time in late September 2026 is EDT (UTC-4). Madrid in September 2026 is on CEST (UTC+2) — the EU shifts to standard time only in late October, so no DST mismatch issue yet.

Difference: CEST is 6 hours ahead of EDT.

5:00 PM ET + 6 hours = 11:00 PM Madrid time, same calendar date (Sept 30, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (no daylight saving time).

July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC minus 5 hours = July 15, 2026, 07:00 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST = UTC+2, Tokyo (JST) = UTC+9, a difference of +7 hours.

June 1, 2026, 9:00 AM CEST + 7 hours = June 1, 2026, 4:00 PM JST.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is 11:59 PM PDT (UTC−7) on Oct 11, 2026.

Converting to UTC: 23:59 + 7h = 06:59 UTC on Oct 12, 2026.

Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2), since EU daylight saving ends Oct 25, 2026.

06:59 UTC + 2h = 08:59 on Oct 12, 2026, Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST is UTC−8. March 3, 2026, 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026, 07:59 UTC.

Madrid in early March 2026 is still on CET (UTC+1), since EU daylight saving starts March 29, 2026. So add 1 hour: 07:59 UTC + 1 = 08:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1 (standard time, no DST in February). So 10:00 CET = 09:00 UTC.

Los Angeles in early February is on PST (UTC−8), since U.S. daylight saving time doesn't start until March.

09:00 UTC − 8 hours = 01:00 PST, same calendar date (February 2, 2026).

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9, Lima (Peru) is UTC-5, a difference of 14 hours (Lima is behind).

May 5, 2026, 8:00 AM JST − 14 hours = May 4, 2026, 6:00 PM Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by late October 2026, since EU DST ends Oct 25, 2026. The US is still on PDT (UTC-7) on Oct 28, 2026, since US DST ends Nov 1, 2026.

11:59 PM PDT (UTC-7) on Oct 28 = 06:59 UTC on Oct 29 = 07:59 CET on Oct 29 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The event is at 9:00 AM ET on October 30, 2026.

- US Eastern Time: DST ends Nov 1, 2026, so Oct 30 is still in EDT (UTC−4).
- Madrid: EU DST ends Oct 25, 2026, so by Oct 30 Madrid is back to standard CET (UTC+1).

Difference: CET is 5 hours ahead of EDT.

9:00 AM EDT + 5 hours = 2:00 PM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1, so 18:00 CET = 17:00 UTC on October 27, 2026.

New York in late October is still on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4), since DST doesn't end until the first Sunday of November.

17:00 UTC − 4 hours = 13:00 EDT, same calendar day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Since November 2, 2026 falls after the US DST change (ends Nov 1, 2026) but before Spain's DST change (ends Oct 25, 2026 — already happened), "PT" here is Pacific Standard Time (UTC−8), and Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

Difference: UTC+1 − UTC−8 = 9 hours ahead.

11:59 PM PST + 9 hours = 8:59 AM the next day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline "11:59 PM PT" refers to Pacific Time. On March 20, 2026, Pacific Daylight Time (UTC-7) is in effect (DST started March 8, 2026 in the US). So 11:59 PM PDT = 06:59 UTC (March 21).

Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) at that date, since EU DST doesn't start until March 29, 2026. Adding 1 hour: 06:59 UTC → 07:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Since the webinar is on March 25, 2026, EU daylight saving hasn't started yet (it begins March 29, 2026), so "CET" is accurate at UTC+1.

12:00 PM CET = 11:00 UTC.

Los Angeles is in PDT (UTC-7) by March 25, 2026 (DST began March 8, 2026).

11:00 UTC − 7 hours = 4:00 AM PDT, same day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Deadline: 12:00 AM ET (EDT, UTC-4) on Oct 12, 2026 = 04:00 UTC on Oct 12, 2026.

Madrid in mid-October 2026 is still on CEST (UTC+2), since DST ends Oct 25, 2026.

04:00 UTC + 2h = 06:00 local time in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) = UTC−12. The deadline (Oct 9, 2026, 23:59 AoE) corresponds to Oct 10, 2026, 11:59 UTC.

Madrid in October 2026 is on CEST (UTC+2), since DST doesn't end until the last Sunday of October (Oct 25, 2026).

So: 11:59 UTC + 2 hours = 13:59 on Oct 10, 2026, Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Pacific Time in August 2026 is PDT (UTC−7). 12:00 PM PDT = 19:00 UTC.
Madrid in August uses CEST (UTC+2), so 19:00 UTC = 21:00 local time, same calendar date.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (India Standard Time) is UTC+5:30. Madrid in November uses CET (UTC+1), since EU daylight saving time ends in late October.

- 23:59 IST (Nov 10, 2026) → convert to UTC: subtract 5:30 → 18:29 UTC (Nov 10, 2026)
- Convert to Madrid time (UTC+1): add 1:00 → 19:29 (Nov 10, 2026)

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45, and Lima (Peru) is UTC−5:00. The difference is 10 hours 45 minutes (Lima is behind).

5:00 PM NPT, April 2, 2026
→ Subtract 10h45m
→ 6:15 AM, April 2, 2026 (Lima time)

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide is on ACDT (UTC+10:30) in October 2026 (DST starts Oct 4). Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) since DST doesn't end until Oct 25, 2026.

10:00 AM ACDT, Oct 6 → UTC: subtract 10:30 → 23:30 UTC, Oct 5.
Convert to Madrid (UTC+2): add 2:00 → 01:30, Oct 6.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is on AEST (UTC+10) on October 3, 2026, since DST begins October 4. So 6:00 PM Sydney = 08:00 UTC.

Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) in early October 2026 (DST ends later in October), so 08:00 UTC = 10:00 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
